identity.title: ALMA Continuum Observations of a 30 Myr Old Gaseous Debris Disk around HD 21997

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we present ALMA and *Herschel Space Observatory* observations of one of these disks, around HD 21997, and study the distribution and origin of the dust and its connection to the gas.

evidence.quote: At a distance of 72 pc, HD 21997 belongs to the 30-Myr-old Columba association

question.value: What is the distribution and origin of the dust in the gaseous debris disk around HD 21997, and how does it relate to the CO gas?

evidence.quote: study the distribution and origin of the dust and its connection to the gas
PI: Á. Kóspál, project ID: 2011.0.00780.S

bands.value: four 2 GHz spectral windows around 345 GHz (effective wavelength 886 um)

evidence.quote: Four spectral windows with bandwidth of 2 GHz each were defined around 345  GHz.
in a compact configuration using 15 antennas
offering baselines from 18.3m to 134.2m
a beam size of 1$\ensuremath{''}$56$\times$1$\ensuremath{''}$26
typical r.m.s noise of 4.5$\times$10$^{-2}$ mJy/beam
The total on-source exposure time was $\approx$2 hr.
Observations were executed on 2011 November 4

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: Own Cycle 0 Early Science program (PI Kóspál)

evidence.quote: as part of our ALMA Early Science Cycle 0 program
We obtained far-infrared and submillimeter maps of HD 21997
covering the $5.2-38\,\mu$m range
A stellar photosphere model with a luminosity of 11.3 L$_\odot$ was taken from (cite: moor2011).

what.value: CO gas disk radii (<26 AU, 138±20 AU) and CO mass 0.04-0.08 Mearth

evidence.quote: inner and outer radii of $<$26 AU and 138$\pm$20 AU
Callisto was used to constrain the absolute amplitude scale.
The uncertainty includes 10% calibration uncertainty.
We performed the imaging with the multi-frequency synthesis (MFS) algorithm with the CASA v3.3

evidence.quote: we extracted the continuum emission from the FDM data using line-free channels, and concatenated these with our TDM measurements using appropriate weighting.
a beam size of 1$\ensuremath{''}$56$\times$1$\ensuremath{''}$26
typical r.m.s noise of 4.5$\times$10$^{-2}$ mJy/beam

evidence.quote: described in (cite: kospal2013)

evidence.quote: the IRS spectra were sampled in 11 adjacent bins using the same method as in (cite: moor2010)

analysis_steps.goal: Image continuum and measure ring geometry and flux

method.value: Fit ellipse to ring intensity maxima along cuts every 10 deg; derive inclination assuming circular ring; aperture photometry

evidence.quote: These points could be fitted with an ellipse having major and minor axes of 2$\ensuremath{''}$06$\times$1$\ensuremath{''}$73

key_parameters.value: aperture radius 2.8 arcsec centered on star

evidence.quote: circular aperture with a radius of 2$\ensuremath{''}$8 centered on the stellar position
Assuming an intrinsically circular ring, we derived an inclination

validation.value: Compared azimuthal scatter with noise and with emission-free ellipses

evidence.quote: We also defined a number of ellipses of the same size and orientation as the fitted one in different emission-free parts of the map.

method.value: Elliptical Gaussian fits with quadratic PSF deconvolution; aperture photometry

evidence.quote: We fitted elliptical Gaussians to the source and PSFs, and used quadratic deconvolution to derive the target’s FWHM sizes

key_parameters.value: PACS aperture 20 arcsec, sky annulus 40-50 arcsec

evidence.quote: aperture radius of 20$''$ and sky annulus between 40$''$ and 50$''$

method.value: Deproject visibilities, bin radially in 7 klambda, fit with DEBRA optically thin model over grid of Rin, Rout, p and smin

evidence.quote: radially averaged in 7 k$\lambda$ wide bins
The maximum grain size ($s_{max}$) was fixed at 3000$\mu$m

assumptions.value: Silicate (olivine) + amorphous carbon, Mie theory, size exponent -3.5

evidence.quote: The dust size distribution was assumed to be power-law with an exponent of $-$3.5

fitting.value: Marginal likelihood estimator from chi2 of grid models

evidence.quote: derived using a marginal likelihood estimator, calculated from the $\chi^2$ of the fit of individual models

validation.value: Model SEDs compared with observations; smin=4 um excluded

evidence.quote: This comparison excluded $s_{min}=4$$\mu$m for its incompatibility with mid-infrared data.

analysis_steps.goal: Extended model with cold outer halo

method.value: Simultaneous fit of SED and ALMA visibilities with equal chi2 weight; PACS image consistency check; ALMA flux excluded from SED

evidence.quote: We combined $\chi^2$ values of the SED and ALMA visibilities with equal weight and performed a consistency check on the PACS images.
We used DEBRA with the same modelling setup as above.

validation.value: Convolved models with PACS PSFs compared to images

evidence.quote: the simulated PACS images – calculated by convolving our model them with the appropriately rotated PACS PSFs
CASA v3.3 (Common Astronomy Software Applications) task CLEAN

used_for.value: radiative transfer modelling of visibilities and SED

evidence.quote: The DEBris disk RAdiative transfer code (cite: olofsson2012), developed for optically thin radiation, was used to model the visibilities.
We reduced the data with HIPE v9.2 using the standard pipeline script.
Spitzer IRS Custom Extraction Software (SPICE v2.5.0)
obtained 2.69$\pm$0.30 mJy for the total continuum flux of the dust disk
inclination of 32.9$^\circ$$\pm$2.6$^\circ$
a P.A. of 21.5$^\circ$$\pm$3.5$^\circ$
$M_{dust}=0.09\pm$0.03 M$_\oplus$
$M_{dust} = 0.27\pm0.11$ M$_\oplus$
Our extended model gives a fractional luminosity of 4.8$\times$10$^{-4}$

findings_qualitative.value: Ring shows no significant azimuthal asymmetry

evidence.quote: there is no observational evidence for any azimuthal asymmetry in the ring.

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA flux is ~30% of SCUBA flux, attributed to filtered extended emission

evidence.quote: we suspect that this flux loss occurred because some extended emission was filtered out by the ALMA interferometer.

claims.hypothesis: Is there a dust-poor inner region where gas still exists?
claims.experiment: Compare dust inner radius from ALMA modelling with CO gas inner radius
claims.result: Rin dust 55±16 AU vs gas <26 AU, 1.8 sigma difference
claims.finding: Probably a dust-poor inner hole with co-located gas and dust only between ~55 and ~140 AU

evidence.quote: implying that probably there is a dust-poor inner region

claims.hypothesis: Is there a cold extended dust outskirt?
claims.experiment: Simultaneous fit of SED, PACS profiles and ALMA visibilities
claims.result: Extended model with Rout>490 AU fits long wavelength data
claims.finding: Cold extended component exists but is weakly constrained

evidence.quote: our modelling suggests the existence of a cold extended component, but its physical parameters are only weakly constrained by our data.

claims.hypothesis: Is the dust in the gaseous disk secondary?
claims.experiment: Compare grain lifetimes with models of gas-dust interaction
claims.result: Grain lifetime <2e4 yr even with gas-to-dust 100
claims.finding: Dust is secondary, replenished by planetesimals, a hybrid disk

evidence.quote: we conclude that the grains must be replenished and are of secondary origin.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Self-stirring cannot explain extent beyond ~90 AU; planetary stirring proposed

evidence.quote: The dust disk (and the planetesimal belt) of HD 21997 extends out to $\gg$90AU, which cannot be explained via self-stirring.

limitations_admitted.value: Details of grain migration cannot be constrained by the data

evidence.quote: the details of grain migration (e.g. the magnitude of migration) cannot be reliably constrained by the available data

referee_caveats_inferred: Only a compact configuration, so extended emission is filtered and the outer halo is poorly constrained
Model grain composition assumed without spectral features

reproducibility.score_reason: Data public in archive and the recipe is described, but imaging and modelling details are sparse.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Recipe lacks imaging and grid details; the DEBRA modelling is not easily redone.
